ads_ratio.reason: The traded Nasdaq price is per ordinary share, the same unit as the EDGAR per-share figures, so the ordinary-shares-per-traded-share ratio is 1.0 and no scaling applies. Declared under step 8(d) bounded authority: the 1:1 relationship is established by the filer's own annual filing (20-F cover + Exhibit 2.1 share description), not by an outside source.
ads_ratio.source: Elbit Systems Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (filed with the SEC on March 17, 2026): the security registered under Section 12 is the ordinary shares (NIS 1 par), described in Exhibit 2.1 to that 20-F; the company's share-capital description states it has one class of Section 12 securities — ordinary shares — registered for trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market and the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange under the symbol ESLT. Elbit has no ADS program: the Nasdaq-traded security IS the ordinary share.

moat_against: Revenue ultimately rests on government defense budgets and procurement cycles — no consumer/commercial pricing power
Fixed-price program execution and capacity-ramp risk as backlog converts; cost overruns land on Elbit
Competes with far larger US and European primes (Lockheed Martin, RTX, Northrop, Rheinmetall) for the same rearmament budgets
Export-license and political risk: scrutiny of Israeli arms exports and Middle East operations can block or delay programs
Controlling shareholder Federmann Enterprises (~41%) — governance concentration; FY2025 equity offering diluted the count
moat_for: Record $32.0B order backlog at Q2 2026 (+34% YoY, ~73% from outside Israel) — multi-year contracted visibility
Broad integrated portfolio across aerospace, C4I/cyber, ISTAR/EW and land — systems-integration switching costs for armed-force customers
Combat-proven differentiated tech: Iron Beam directed energy, Hermes UAVs, electro-optics/electronic warfare
Incumbent supplier to the Israeli MoD and localized manufacturing/partnerships inside NATO markets (e.g. Serbia JV, European programs)
moat_justification: Israel's largest defense contractor with a broad, integrated portfolio (aerospace, C4I/cyber, ISTAR & electronic warfare, land systems, US subsidiary), combat-proven systems (Iron Beam laser, Hermes UAVs, electro-optics) and a record $32.0B backlog at Q2 2026 giving multi-year revenue visibility — against government-budget dependence, fixed-price execution and capacity-ramp risk, competition from far larger US/European primes, export-license and political scrutiny of Israeli arms sales, and a controlling shareholder (Federmann Enterprises, ~41% per S&P via a May 2026 6-K). Pricing power is real but capped by government contracting; returns have been earned through a demand supercycle, not yet proven through a downturn.
name: Elbit Systems Ltd
one_liner: Quality defense franchise, moat 6/10, record $32.0B backlog — but at $698.72 the price is far beyond any owner's-earnings DCF: weighted IRR 4.3%, weighted IV@15% $88.60 on the normalized base of $6.80/share (latest FY $11.22/share still leaves IV far below price); clears the 15% hurdle only below ~$89.
